name: dot-stepper
title: Dot stepper
description: Page dots for onboarding, carousels and short flows: the current dot stretches into a pill, each dot can be a button, and past seven a window slides.
docs: count is how many steps there are and value the current one, counted from 0. Give it onValueChange and every dot becomes a button inside a list (label names the list, 'Steps' by default); each button is named 'Step 3 of 5' and, with labels (one name per dot: ['Welcome', 'Invite your team', ...]), 'Step 2 of 5, Invite your team'; the current one is marked aria-current='step'. Without onValueChange the dots are one picture with a single name, 'Step 2 of 5' (format changes the words; {current} and {total} are the numbers, and a label is added for the current step). The current dot stretches into a pill and the others stay small. Past seven dots the row no longer grows: a window of five slides along as value moves, the dots at its edges shrink to say there is more, and the dots outside the window are hidden and cannot be tabbed to; each button still knows its place in the whole (aria-posinset and aria-setsize). size is sm, md or lg and orientation horizontal or vertical. The dots, and the focus ring, are drawn in currentColor, so a dark photo takes text-white and shows a white ring. As buttons the dots sit 24px apart, so each button is a 24 by 24px target (WCAG 2.5.8); as a picture they sit closer. A dot that is not current is half strength, and the focus ring has room inside the clip. The stretch and the slide are instant under reduced motion. It keeps no state of its own: it is a view of value.
